patch_description: Fundamentally different approach: instead of hill-climbing discrete center positions with an LP radius solver, treat the packing as a continuous optimization problem with radii and centers as joint decision variables. Maximize sum(r) + penalty for overlaps and wall violations using a penalty method with L-BFGS-B gradient descent. The penalty P = Σ relu(r_i + r_j - d_ij)² + Σ relu(r_i - wall_i)² has simple analytic gradients w.r.t. both centers and radii. Anneal the penalty weight high→low so the solution converges to a feasible packing while pushing radii up. Use a good hex seed plus random restarts with jitter. This should outperform hill-climbing because it can move all 52 variables simultaneously along the true objective gradient, escaping the coordinate-wise limitations, and it's fast (each L-BFGS-B run is milliseconds).
